coverage.evidence: -Units that were constructed within the last 15 years (this applies on a rolling basis – i.e.. a unit constructed on January 1, 2006 is not covered as of January, 1 2020, but is covered on and after January 1, 2021).
coverage.note: The 15-year cutoff is supported. The two-unit owner-occupied exemption is stated (second unit occupied by an owner for the entire tenancy), but the card's 'max units 2' is a loose rendering.

citation.note: AB 1482 is named, and Civil Code 1947.12(d)(5)(B)(i) is cited for the single-family exemption. The page does not cite 1947.12 as the source of the cap.

requirement.evidence: In order to apply to a tenancy, it requires that the tenant either has lived in the same unit for at least six months or that their original lease expired, whichever comes first.
requirement.note: The page also covers at-fault and no-fault reasons and relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

key_value.evidence: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

effective_date.evidence: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).
effective_date.note: March 27, 2023 is the effective date of the non-payment threshold rule, not of the JCO itself. The page gives no JCO effective date.
